name: store_flood
kind: service-axis measurement of the SM global-store path in steady state (store buffer full); no workload-based fitting
question: When global stores are issued faster than one SM can hand them to L2, what does one request cost the SM's store path as a function of the distinct 32-B sectors and distinct 128-B lines its lanes touch, the store width and the number of issuing warps, and how many requests does the SM buffer before the issuing warp stalls (lg_throttle)?
motivation: Full-gpu cases with a per-element STG epilogue (H100 cutlass cp.async / sparse GEMM, B300 CuTe-DSL software-pipelined GEMM, FMHA MLA) spend 59-82 (H100) and 145-170 (B300) warp-cycles per STG against 30-33 and 72-98 in the engine (fg-over20 notes, 2026-11-13). The engine charges the SM store port one sector at store_l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle (1.0 cycle per sector on both devices) and gates STG issue on store_l2.outstanding_requests (H100 43, B300 256, the latter a carried-over value never measured). store_scatter r1 kept 24 gaps per window; its few saturated tails were not interpreted (addendum: 'late gaps show geometry-dependent buffering/service and remain a separate investigation').
probe: store_flood.cu. One CTA on one SM, W warps (warp w on SMSP w % 4), bar.sync + fence.sc.gpu before every window. Window = N = 384 global stores per warp issued back to back in an unrolled group of G = 8 stores followed by one %clock64 read (48 groups); the store address of group g, slot k, lane l is base + ((g * 8 + k) * 8 + warp) * 4096 + l * stride, so every request owns a fresh 4-KiB region and no two requests share a line. Lanes l >= L do not store (predicated). Variants: width 2 (st.global.u16), 4 (st.global.b32), 8 (st.global.v2.b32), 16 (st.global.v4.b32); lane stride in {width, 32, 64, 128} bytes; active lanes L in {8, 16, 32}; W in {1, 2, 4, 8}; a clock-only control (no store). Lane 0 of every warp records the 49 stamps. Destination buffer 8 warps * 384 * 4096 B = 12.6 MiB, zeroed by the host before every launch. Runs a and b, 8 launches * 17 repetitions each, repetition 0 discarded.
cells: Full cross only where it separates the terms: width 4 with stride {4, 32, 64, 128} x L {8, 16, 32} x W {1, 2, 4, 8}; widths 2 and 8 with stride {width, 32, 128}, L 32, W {2, 8}; width 16 with stride {16, 32, 128}, L 32, W {2, 8}; control W {1, 8}. sectors and lines of a cell are computed from (width, stride, L) by the model script.

controls.sass: Per kernel: 49 SR_CLOCKLO reads; exactly 8 STG of the declared width between neighbouring reads (0 for the control); no load, barrier, branch or other memory instruction inside a group other than the loop back-edge between groups; address arithmetic only adds immediates to one pointer register per group.
controls.timing: Runs a and b agree on the steady gap within max(2 cycles, 10 %). The early gap (groups 2..3) of the contiguous cells reproduces the installed storage.global.store_issue intervals (8 stores * 3 / 3 / 6 / 23 cycles for width 2 / 4 / 8 / 16) within max(4 cycles, 15 %). The control's group gap is the loop overhead and is subtracted.
controls.steady: A cell counts as saturated when the median gap of groups 33..48 exceeds 1.5 times its early gap and groups 33..40 and 41..48 agree within 10 %. Unsaturated cells give the issue interval only and do not enter the service fit.

derivation: Per run and cell: gap medians per group; steady interval per request of one warp I = median(gaps 33..48) / 8 minus the control's per-store overhead; SM-level service per request T = I / W. Buffer: knee group = first group whose gap exceeds 1.5 times the early gap; requests outstanding at the knee = W * 8 * knee - (elapsed cycles at the knee) / T. Fit T = a * sectors + b * lines + c over the saturated cells of one device (least squares, all widths together; then per width to see whether width enters).

predictions_before_data.h100: From the three saturated cells of store_scatter h100-r1 (stride 128: 64 cycles per request and warp pair -> 128 at W = 2, 64 at W = 1; stride 32: 80 at W = 2): T = 1.0 * sectors + 1.0 * lines (a = b = 1, c = 0) within 15 %, independent of width; I = W * T (one service per SM shared by its SMSPs). Buffer 36-43 requests for width <= 8.
predictions_before_data.b300: From store_scatter b300-r1 (width 16 and 8, stride 32 and 128 at W = 2: 64 per warp): a = 1.0, b between 0 and 0.5 (not determined); buffer about 40 requests for width <= 8, not the installed 256.
predictions_before_data.falsifiers: T not proportional to W at fixed geometry (per-SMSP rather than per-SM service); T depending on width at fixed (sectors, lines); a buffer that scales with bytes instead of requests.

outcomes_before_data.install: If the fit reproduces every saturated cell within 15 % (or 3 cycles): add the per-line term to the SM store port (new field of memory.store_l2.service, cycles per distinct line of a request) and set store_l2.outstanding_requests of each device to the measured buffer; evidence level experimental until the engine replay below passes, measured after.
outcomes_before_data.partial: If only a subset of geometries fits (for example width 16), install nothing for the rest and write an addendum naming what the fit does not cover.
outcomes_before_data.none: If the SASS or timing controls fail, repair the probe first.

prediction_check: Replay through tracer -> convert -> engine of at least four saturated cells per device (two geometries x W in {2, 8}) with the candidate leaves: simulated steady interval per request within 15 % of hardware. Then the full-gpu 500 x 2 regression against main's baseline (fg-line-cold/full-df).
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing, no tuning a measured value to the full-gpu error, no treating instrumented probe output as hardware timing. Any post-data change of a criterion is labelled as such with its reason.

addenda.when: before any run (probe not yet written)
addenda.text: Active lanes: instead of predicating lanes l >= L off, lane l stores to the address and with the value of lane l mod L (the lane term of the address is (l mod L) * stride). The request then touches exactly the sectors and lines of L lanes, and the timed window contains no predicate or branch. The model script computes sectors and lines from (width, stride, L) accordingly.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/store_flood/{h100-r1,b300-r1}); SASS gate passed on both, runs a / b agree on every steady gap within 3.6 % / 2.7 %
addenda.text: The predicted form T = a * sectors + b * lines is REJECTED as written: contiguous requests that write whole sectors show no line term (h100 w16.s16.l32: 16 sectors in 4 lines, T = 15.9; w8.s8.l32 7.9; w4.s4.l32 3.9). What the saturated cells follow instead (form changed after seeing the data, stated as such): T = max(floor, sectors + P) per request and SM, P = number of touched 128-B lines that contain a partially written granule; granule = 32 B on h100 (a sector written in part: w4 / w16 at stride 32 / 64 / 128 give sectors + lines, e.g. w16.s32.l32 32 sectors in 8 lines = 39.9, w4.s64.l8 8 in 4 = 11.8), 4 B on b300 (only the width-2 cells carry the term: w2.s128.l32 66.5 = 32 + 32, w2.s32.l32 39.9 = 32 + 8; width 4 / 8 / 16 give T = sectors: w4.s32.l32 31.9, w4.s128.l32 31.9 at W = 2 / 4, w16.s32.l32 31.9). Against this rule: h100 74 of 74 saturated (run, cell) pairs within 3.4 % (criterion 15 %); b300 62 of 64 within 15 %, the two exceptions are w4.s128.l16.x1 in both runs (+26 %; stride-128 cells at W = 1 read 21.6 / 35.9 for 16 / 32 sectors while W = 2 / 4 read 15.9-17.8 / 31.9; not explained, not modelled). T is proportional to W at fixed geometry on both devices (one service per SM), independent of width at fixed geometry except through the granule. Whether the h100 granule is the sector or the line is decided by the unsaturated cell w4.s4.l16.x4 (two whole sectors, half a line): 7.75 cycles per store and warp = 1.94 per request, which excludes sectors + 1 = 3. Floor: one- and two-sector requests settle at 1.94 (W = 4) / 2.0-2.09 (W = 8) cycles per request on both devices -> 2.0. Buffer (requests outstanding at the knee; coarse, groups of 8): h100 W = 1 / 2 / 4 medians 32.6 / 39.5 / 61.4, b300 30.2 / 35.6 / 59.3; it counts requests (no trend with 8-32 sectors) and grows with the number of issuing SMSPs; the installed h100 value 43 lies inside this range and is kept, the b300 value 256 (carried over, never measured) is replaced by the W = 4 median 59. Install (experimental until the replay of the prediction check passes): store_l2.partial_line_cycles = 1.0 with store_l2.partial_granule_bytes = 32 (h100) / 4 (b300), store_l2.issue_interval_cycles = 2.0 (both), b300 store_l2.outstanding_requests = 59. Scope: lane stores (STG) only; TMA / bulk stores, reductions and atomics were not in the probe and keep their present cost. Not covered: the b300 W = 1 stride-128 excess, the W dependence of the buffer, W = 8 buffer (those cells are saturated from the first group).

addenda.when: after the engine replay and two full-gpu regressions (2026-11-13)
addenda.text: Replay (H100, tracer -> convert -> engine, 4 cells): with the leaves of the previous addendum the SM-level service matched but the per-warp interval was 0.50 (W = 2) / 0.25 (W = 4) of hardware: the engine let one warp drain its whole window while the others waited; hardware interleaves the blocked warps (every warp's group gap is W x T). Engine change (no leaf): warps blocked at the store-buffer gate are admitted in arrival order per SM; replay after it: 1.005-1.012 on all four cells ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/sflood-replay2-table.txt), criterion 15 % met. Limit of the partial-line term found in real kernels: the probe gives every request fresh lines; a GEMM epilogue's next STG fills the other bytes of the sectors the previous one wrote in part. cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_00 (4 epilogue warps, STG.E.U16, 4 partly written sectors in 4 lines per request): hardware 5.05 cycles per request at SM level (PC sampling, lg_throttle region), engine 4 without the term and 8 with it; the full-gpu ratio of that case went 1.04 -> 1.21 and eight other accurate cutlass GEMM cases moved from 0.94-1.06 to 1.07-1.19. The term as measured therefore holds for first writes to a line and is NOT installed for general use: store_l2.partial_line_cycles is set to 0 on both devices (field, engine code and CTest stay; a refill cell - consecutive requests completing the same sectors - is needed before it can be installed). Kept: admission order, issue floor 2.0 for lane stores, b300 outstanding_requests 59.
